items.title: Marty Grosz interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 4, 1995
items.q: I remember my first jazz record I ever bought for myself was a Commodore Record called “Paging the Devil” ... by Lester Young, Buck Clayton, and the Kansas City Six I think it was.

ctx.x: Yeah, I’ve got this cool thing here. Yeah it’s a whole new tune when you start harmonizing. © Fillius Jazz Archive -4-

Yeah. You start putting in diminished chords in the middle and all kinds of stuff, you know, re-harmonizing it and so forth. And so I’m actually a product of a guy who heard records, and heard some bands, saw some bands, and wanted to play. As opposed to the other kind of guy who, like the piano players, who had started playing, or violin, kids who’d play on violin, they’d play violin for two or three years and stuff, and all of a sudden they discover jazz. Or somebody says “you know you can make some money…
